list.item: Two months of tiredness, easy bruising and bleeding gums, with pancytopenia and 12 percent blasts on the blood smear; acute leukemia suspected and urgent hematology review booked: active, confirmed [S]

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over about four decades: X-ray work early in her career, laboratory work with polonium and other radioactive sources, and a laboratory accident in which a sealed polonium source ruptured on her bench about ten years ago: active, confirmed [S]
Pulmonary tuberculosis in her forties, treated to completion; no symptoms of active disease: active, confirmed [S]

Urgent evaluation of pancytopenia with blasts on the smear: peripheral smear review, comprehensive metabolic panel, LDH and uric acid today; coagulation tests at the hematology visit; no aspirin or anti-inflammatory drugs; go to the emergency department at once for a temperature of 38.0 °C or more, bleeding that does not stop, or new confusion or headache. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Acute Myeloid Leukemia, Version 5.2026 (2026) [S]

Urgent hematology/oncology consultation within two days for suspected acute leukemia: bone marrow biopsy, classification and treatment plan. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Acute Myeloid Leukemia, Version 5.2026 (2026) [S]

Occupational health history: her work with X-rays, polonium and other sources over about four decades, and the sealed-source accident in her laboratory, documented; written request to the employer's radiation safety office for her dosimetry and bioassay records, which the employer must keep and must furnish on request. Guideline: 10 CFR 19.13, Notifications and reports to individuals (radiation exposure reports on request) (2026); 29 CFR 1910.1096, Ionizing radiation (records of exposure and disclosure to employees) (2026) [S]
